historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (rounded); equity CAGR understates the business because buybacks ($0.8-1.2B/yr) shrink book
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.1% vs EPS 5yr 30.4% (FY2020 COVID trough base, EPS $1.36) and equity 3yr 3.5% vs EPS 3yr 8.3%: divergence driven by buybacks (shares ~226M FY2020 -> ~172M) and the COVID base. Revenue CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (reported FCF less SBC) track reported FCF closely (SBC ~0.5-0.6% of revenue), so SBC is not funding the growth. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is negative because FY2022 ($1,068M) was a peak cash year and FY2024 had the Wichita strike; the 5yr figure starts from the FY2020 COVID trough. Neither is a forward guide; the build is from components.

scenario_narratives.base: Textron converts its $18.9B backlog at roughly the 5% revenue CAGR of the last five years: FY2026 +6% (H1 +7.1%, guided adjusted EPS $6.40-6.60), then 5% as Bell's MV-75 ramps from engineering-and-manufacturing development toward low-rate production and Citation deliveries hold up on Ascend/Longitude demand, decelerating to 3% by year 8. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs from 9.6% to ~11.7% as Aviation captures its ~$150M productivity opportunity and Bell's mix moves from lower-margin MV-75 development work to production; FY2027 is held back ~20bp for separation and stranded corporate cost. MV-75 factory capex keeps capex at 3.4% of revenue for two years, and the FY2026 reprogramming request is assumed received, as guidance assumes. The Industrial separation is value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: MV-75 is funded on schedule and turns Bell into a growth business for the next decade (the ~$70B lifetime program value starts to flow), the business-jet upcycle extends with Citation aftermarket compounding on a larger fleet, and the pure-play aerospace & defense company runs at ~13% EBITDA margin by year 6. Growth runs 7% for three years before fading to 3%. No re-rating is credited: the upside is flows, not multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The business-jet cycle turns: corporate profits and used-aircraft values soften from FY2027, Citation deliveries fall and revenue declines 2% in year 3 with margin dropping to ~8.4% on under-absorption. In parallel MV-75 appropriations slip (management already flags $0.20-0.30 of EPS and $150-250M of cash at risk on the FY26 reprogramming alone), Bell carries the Fort Worth factory without the volume, and the Industrial separation leaves ~40bp of stranded cost. Recovery to ~9.6% margin and 2.5-3% growth only from year 5. Inventory-heavy working capital consumes 18% of incremental revenue.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated manufacturing business on owner FCF (SBC expensed, share count flat), with the captive Finance group and a haircut pension surplus added in the bridge and manufacturing net debt deducted. The Industrial separation is treated as value-neutral (no conglomerate-discount unwind is credited), so any re-rating of the pure-play aerospace & defense remainco is upside to this model, not in it. Terminal value is capped at 14x FCF for a cyclical with a defense core.
key_risks_to_valuation: Business-jet cycle: Aviation is ~41% of revenue and most of the profit growth
MV-75/FLRAA funding and execution: the Bell growth and margin path depends on annual Army appropriations
Separation execution: structure (spin vs sale), tax leakage on a sale, stranded costs
Cash-tax normalization: FY2025 cash taxes were 9% of pretax; the ramp to 19% is an assumption
Pension surplus credit (35% of $2.6B) depends on rates and on Textron being able to use it

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (txt-20260103.htm) AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $81M; no separate equity-award tax-withholding line is disclosed in financing activities, so no addition. FY2023 $94M, FY2024 $66M.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest 31 December (52/53-week; FY2025 was 53 weeks, ended 2026-01-03)
inputs.share_count_basis: 171.99M basic shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-17) plus ~1.5M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted 175.006M less basic 173.500M weighted) = 173.5M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks ($822M FY2025, $377M H1-2026, 4.1M shares) are what keeps it flat and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity 9.5% (10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (Textron senior notes ~5% x (1-21%)); market-value weights ~79/21 (equity 173.5M x $77 = $13.4B; manufacturing debt $3.5B) -> 8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality and MV-75 funding risk are carried in the bear flows and its 20% weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost already sits inside operating expense (segment profit), so the lease is charged in the flows; the $406M operating lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B). No finance leases of consequence.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US cyclical industrial/aerospace-defense; routing table row 2 with the cyclical adaptations: risk charged once, one lease treatment, matching-asset rule for the Finance group and pension). First valuation of TXT (no MEMORY entry). STRUCTURE: Textron reports a Manufacturing group and a Finance group. Flows and net debt are MANUFACTURING ONLY: net debt = manufacturing debt $3,466M (current $355M + long-term $3,111M) less manufacturing cash $1,436M at 2026-07-04 (Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet / debt-to-capital table). The captive Finance group (cash $170M, receivables $524M, debt $339M) is carried at book equity in the equity bridge, its segment profit excluded from the EBITDA path. SEPARATION: the April-2026 announced separation of Industrial (Kautex + Specialized Vehicles, ~$3B revenue, ~5% segment margin) is modelled as value-neutral to holders (a tax-free spin hands them the Industrial shares; a sale converts it to cash), so the build is the CONSOLIDATED continuing company including Industrial. What is charged: one-off separation costs (~$100M) and stranded corporate cost as ~20bp lower FY2027 margin in base, a permanent ~40bp hit in bear; no re-rating credit is taken anywhere. FY0 = FY2025 (53 weeks), so FY2026 growth of 6% is net of a ~1.5-2pt 53rd-week comp (H1-2026 revenue +7.1% YoY). EBITDA margin anchor: FY2025 manufacturing segment profit $1,314M - corporate $149M - LIFO provision $199M (treated as a real inflation cost) + D&A ex intangible amortization $369M + SBC $81M = $1,416M = 9.6% of revenue, pre-SBC. Non-service pension income is excluded from the flows (non-cash). Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes were $104M (9% of $1,137M pretax) on restored R&D expensing; ramped from 14% to 19% (book ETR guided ~18%). Working capital: inventory-heavy OEM (inventories $4.7B, 32% of revenue) partly offset by customer deposits; wc_capture -15% of incremental revenue. FY2026 year-1 unlevered owner FCF ~$0.65-0.7B sits near guided manufacturing cash flow before pension of $700-800M plus after-tax interest, less SBC; the dip vs FY2025 ($848M levered owner FCF) is MV-75 working capital and the $632M Fort Worth MV-75 factory in capex (3.4% of revenue FY26-27 vs 2.6% FY25). BUYBACKS: a funded repurchaser, so the flat share count is paid for in cash. TotalDebt in the Metrics CSV is NULL (Textron does not use the us-gaap debt tags); the debt figures here are read from the 10-Q text.

bear.narrative: Business-jet downturn from FY2027, MV-75 appropriations slip, separation leaves stranded cost.

base.narrative: Backlog-supported mid-single-digit growth; Aviation productivity and MV-75 moving from development to production lift margin ~2pt over five years.

bull.narrative: MV-75 funded on schedule into full-rate production, business-jet upcycle extends, Aviation hits its ~200bp productivity target.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): business-jet demand is late in a multi-year upcycle and the MV-75 ramp depends on annual Army appropriations that management itself flags as at risk this year. Base 50%: backlog and guidance support the central path. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs MV-75 funding, an extended jet cycle and the Aviation margin program to all land together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
